newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash grades take firmer stance late Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash grades take firmer stance late Friday.

text.p: U.S. cash grades were finishing off an active week on the firmer side Friday, finding support from an uptick in refiner demand.
Crude traders said both sweet and sour crude differentials narrowed their respective discounts to the April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark.
"A lot of crude was sold, mainly because people wanted to fill out their schedules before the NPRA's start and the expiration of April futures on Thursday," said a trader.
April WTI/Cushing gained all session to talk late at $21.25-35, some 60 cents firmer.
The National Petroleum Refiners Association will start their annual meeting Sunday in San Antonio, Texas, prompting many traders to clean their desks before departing for the conference.
Active buying brought Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James 5-7 cts higher at the late stages Friday, talked at WTI/Cushing -18 to -20 cts,
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was steady at WTI/Cushing -50 to -55 cts, with Midland/WTI narrowly higher at a 30-34 cts discount to the marker.
Sour grades saw West Texas Sour/Midland trade late at WTI/Cushing -$2.58, 5 cts stronger than last deals on Thursday.
Eugene Island was steady at WTI/Cushing -$2.50.
April Postings fluctuated widely, gaining 15 cts on the Apr/May roll to talk late at $1.78-83.
